taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: low much-branched shrub commonly about 3 dm. high; the Range Plant Handbook (p. B36): usually 3 to 12 inches on the range, kept as the low.

traits.height_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 414), Calliandra eriophylla: a straggling shrub up to 1.2 m high (the Range Plant Handbook, p. B36: to 2 feet).

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: a shrub.

traits.woodiness.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 413), Calliandra: stems woody, more than 20 cm long, with stout rigid branches.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: drought-deciduous: it drops its leaflets in the dry fore-summer and leafs again after rain.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: much-branched shrub, no rosette.

traits.bark_colour.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: older branches grey; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves alternate, as in the genus.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra: leaves bipinnate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra: leaves bipinnate.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra: bipinnate: divided twice.

traits.pinnae.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: pinnae 1-7 pairs; most leaves in the photos have 2 to 4 pairs, as the Range Plant Handbook (p. B36) has it (2 or more pairs).

traits.leaflets.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: leaflets 5-8 pairs on each pinna.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: leaflets in pairs.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: leaflets oblong, 3-4 mm. long; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 413) give up to 7 mm, kept as the high.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 413), Calliandra: leaflets 1-2 mm wide, grey-pubescent.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 1 cm to 4 cm long with their pinnae.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: leaflets oblong.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaflets entire, as in the genus.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 413), Calliandra: leaflets grey-pubescent.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: flowers in few-flowered heads, racemose or axillary.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Four to ten flowers in a head, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 110245298, 98659543, 73738608, 271815163, 18298212, 112166239, 15141059, 157608932): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Powder-puff heads 3 cm to 5 cm across with their stamens, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 110245298, 98659543, 73738608, 271815163, 18298212, 112166239, 15141059, 157608932): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: flowers reddish purple; sRGB by eye from the photos (the head reads as its rose-pink stamens).

traits.petal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: corolla 4-6 mm. long.

traits.stamen_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: stamens about 2 cm. long; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 413): about 20 mm.

traits.stamen_exsertion.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: stamens about 2 cm. long from a corolla 4-6 mm. long: far exserted.

traits.filament_colour.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. B36, False-mesquite: stamens purplish; sRGB by eye from the photos (rose-pink to red).

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: legume pubescent.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: legume 3-6 cm. long.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: legume about 5 mm. wide.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 414), Calliandra eriophylla: 5,000 feet or lower, very common on dry gravelly slopes and mesas, February to May (the Range Plant Handbook, p. B36: again after summer rains).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: pods ripen and split from April to June, after the spring flowering.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 414), Calliandra eriophylla: 5,000 feet or lower: about 1,520 m.

traits.light.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 414), Calliandra eriophylla: dry gravelly slopes and mesas, in the open.

traits.moisture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 414), Calliandra eriophylla: dry gravelly slopes and mesas.

traits.soil_texture.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 475, Calliandra eriophylla: rocky canyons and hillsides.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, twiggy, grey shrub with feathery bipinnate leaves and round puffs of long rose-pink to red stamens in spring.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for fairy duster from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of Scotch broom (cytisus-scoparius); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.4 m tall at 10 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada, Tucson Mountain District, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles (1942) and Abrams, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from the library's rules for the form.
